Change: WhiteningTransform.transposeMatrix(plan, input): Either[ArError, DMat] is the true adjoint W^T of matrix(plan, _), not inverse whitening. Each segment and column is reversed independently: seed ebar from input; for t descending, z = s_t * ebar_t (the scale multiplies the fully accumulated ebar, before MA propagation), ybar_t += z, ybar_{t-l} -= phi_l z, ebar_{t-l} -= theta_l z, lags within the segment only. Rows and per-segment firstScale are validated with the forward map's typed errors before any output. Scratch is one Array of the longest segment length; input is read logically through strides and never mutated. Forward code is byte-unchanged. No new dependency or solver in main code.
Evidence via ROOT/run-sbt.py:
- logs/ar-adjoint-final.log (SHA-256 b5c3ee2430321abe8e24e8cd38371f9ab89076e9f379a73d3320507d0078fe04, meta exit 0, 241.2 s): arJVM and arJS testOnly WhiteningTransposeSuite (7 new) + WhiteningPlanSuite (12 existing) = 19/19 each; scalafimCompileAll success with 0 [warn].
- Planted bugs (logs/ar-adjoint-mutantA.log, -mutantB.log): scaling the raw input before MA accumulation fails 3/7 new tests; dropping reverse MA propagation fails 3/7. Source restored; hashes re-verified after the final run.
- Earlier logs/ar-adjoint-r1.log failed -Werror on two unused loop variables in the test; fixed by threading the case name into assertion clues (r2 and final are clean).
Oracle: independent dense W = (I + S B)^-1 S A from the defining equations, via Gale's dense solve, first checked against production forward. Cases: IID; AR(1) exact; AR(3); MA(2); ARMA(2,1) scale 0.6; ARMA(1,2) scale 0; by-run AR(1)/ARMA. They cover global/by-run, two runs, and a censoring reset within a run. Also: dot-product law; zero-scale singular rows; strided/NaN-padded views bit-identical, input unchanged, zero columns; typed row/zero-row/negative-scale/by-run-count refusals.
Not covered: no consumer conditional operator, ML, scientific or performance claim; no full ar module suite beyond these two plus compileAll.
